newsitem.title: UK: GrandMet and Guinness see way out of spirits bind.
newsitem.headline: GrandMet and Guinness see way out of spirits bind.

text.p: The merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc will create a powerful spirits division able to attack difficult market conditions, said John McGrath, named as chief executive of the combined group, to be called GMG Brands.
"Something needs to happen in the spirits industry because it is so fragmented," McGrath told reporters.

"What we have done as industry leaders is recognise that fact and take action which ensures that we get the benefits of the reductions in cost and increasing influence if we are going to be a global player and ensure that the transaction is done in such a way that it is consistent with growing shareholder value."

He said bringing together United Distillers, Guinness' spirits arm, with International Distillers and Vintners (UDV), GrandMet's spirits division, was a "logical response to the environment we face in the worldwide spirits industry".
Many developed markets suffer from declining margins and overcapacity and powerful retailers, he said.
"Developing markets in contrast have exciting long-term growth potential but there is a need for critical mass to support the marketing and infrastructure investment," said McGrath.

Both groups recognise also that the vast majority of cost-savings will be at UDV. They estimate savings at 175 million stg in the third year of trading and about two-thirds of this amount in the second year.
About 50 percent of the cost savings will come from integrating national sales forces and back offices of the two spirits businesses in markets where both groups are active.

Another 20 percent of the expected savings will be achieved by pruning staff and resources at central head offices and regional offices of of the spirits businesses. An additional 20 percent will come from savings in production and purchasing.
But these savings do not assume any benefit from closer integration of UDV with Moet Hennessy LMVH.PA, an associate of UDV.
Guinness and Moet Hennessy have set up a number of joint ventures around the world which handle Guinness' scotch Whisky and gin and Moet's champagne and cognac.

UDV, created by the merger of the spirits operations of GrandMet and Guinness, will have annual spirits sales of over 100 million cases and combined operating profits of more than 1.3 billion stg, McGrath said.
It will also be the largest in the world in terms of case volume and profits, although it will only hold a five-percent share of the world spirits market.
"While size is not enough in itself, it is a start for future growth," McGrath said. -- Tim Farrand,London newsroom +44 171 542 6437
